749e6fc43f9adc4c: SHANGHAI: Carlos Alcaraz fell to Zizou Bergs in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters on Monday, interrupting the former world number one's in-form return to the professional Tour after being sidelined for months by injury.
The 39th-ranked Belgian beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round to land the tournament's biggest upset yet, and will play Tommy Paul next.
"Today wasn't a good match from my side. I didn't feel good," Alcaraz told reporters, crediting Bergs for taking chances and serving big.
"In a few important moments I didn't play my best, and I would say there were a few moments that he was lucky," the 23-year-old said of their two-hour battle.
Alcaraz said he was "disappointed" by a loss riddled with errors, which came a week after he won the Tokyo Open, adding he would return home and hit practice.
"Right now, you know, all the negative thoughts come to my mind and none of the positives, but I think I will take it, you know, the good things," he said.

His loss also ensures current world number two Alexander Zverev, the reigning French Open and US Open champion, will replace Jannik Sinner as world number one by the year's end, with the Italian's season over due to a knee injury.
Zverev, the top seeded player in Shanghai, will face Alexander Bublik in the last 16 on Tuesday.
- 'Disbelief' -
Alcaraz started with more quality until Bergs broke the Spaniard's serve to go up 3-2 in the first set.
Alcaraz grabbed back that break in the next game but was uncharacteristically off-target, sending a mess of shots into the net.
He double-faulted to hand Bergs a critical break point in the 11th game, and lost the first set when a volley went short.

Alcaraz, currently ranked third in the world, was visibly frustrated during the second set as he vented to his corner following a series of misfired shots that left him with no points in the fourth and eighth games.
He forced a tie-break but could not reach a third set as Bergs closed things out on the first match point.
"It's a little disbelief and not feeling too much," Bergs, 27, said after winning.
"You're just really in the moment, being focused on the points you have to play," he said.
- Fritz fumbles -
Earlier, Stefanos Tsitsipas came back to beat Taylor Fritz 3-6, 7-5, 6-3 and earn fourth round meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who brushed aside qualifier Dalibor Svrcina 6-2, 6-3.
A wardrobe malfunction delayed victory for the Greek world number 43 when a tennis ball tumbled out of the American's pocket a second time and forced the men to replay a match point.
A tired-looking Fritz, seeded 11th, hung on for a bit longer to save the eighth game but could not stick around beyond that, with Tsitsipas holding serve to win at the fifth time of asking.
"I could have done a few things easier, but I ended up being my biggest enemy," Tsitsipas told the crowd afterwards.
"I turned things around really well towards the end and became friends with myself and played some incredible tennis," he said.
Felix Auger-Aliassime, Casper Ruud and Rafael Jodar also went through to the last 16.
American world number 18 Paul sent off last year's winner Valentin Vacherot 6-4, 6-2 while Botic van de Zandschulp beat eighth-seeded Arthur Fils 7-5, 6-4.

7e50270697791bb6: PARIS: Two paintings by impressionist master Pierre-Auguste Renoir, stolen from a museum in southern France and later discovered hidden behind a wall, have sustained slight damage, prosecutors said on Monday.
In September, thieves broke into the museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer and escaped with two works by Renoir, abandoning two others as they fled.
The value of all four paintings had been estimated at nine million euros ($10 million).
On Friday, authorities announced that the two outstanding stolen works had been found.
They were a portrait titled "Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano" and a depiction of a woman at a well called "Young Woman at the Well."
Speaking to reporters in Paris, Marseille prosecutor Nicolas Bessone said the paintings were recovered last Thursday during a search of a home in the southern town of Clermont-l'Herault.
The discovery of the stolen works followed the arrest of six people, including a woman, last Wednesday, said Bessone.
"The paintings were hidden behind a solid cinderblock wall. They were completely undetectable," Bessone said.
"It was through interrogation work that investigators were able to get the receiver of the stolen goods to admit that he had indeed taken possession of the paintings."
A 29-year-old man seen as the main suspect was charged at the weekend after DNA evidence linked him to the theft.

The two paintings were "in relatively good condition", although "the two works showed signs of damage," Bessone said, speaking alongside the head of France's national judicial police, Christian Sainte.
The frame of "Young Woman at the Well" was slightly damaged, while "the canvas of 'Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano' had a tear," Bessone said.
The tear was located "on the dress" in the portrait, the prosecutor said, adding that both paintings "will require restoration work."
LATEST HEIST
Culture Minister Catherine Pegard praised "the efficiency and determination of all those who made this outcome possible."
"Their commitment made it possible to recover these works in record time," the culture ministry said.
A spate of heists at French museums – including at the Louvre – has highlighted inadequate security in some cases and led to questions about whether criminal gangs see them as soft targets.
Crown jewels valued at around $100 million were stolen in broad daylight from the Louvre in Paris last year.
While the four suspected Louvre robbers were arrested, the jewels they are accused of grabbing in the seven-minute heist have still not been found.

5adf65b3cedaf1bd: KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched for five missing people on Monday, a day after devastating flash floods swept away more than 200 houses and five bridges along the Budhi Gandaki river.
Videos showed a dark, debris-filled river surging through the hills in central Nepal's Gorkha district.
No deaths have been confirmed.
On Sunday, 95 people including nine foreigners were rescued.
"We are continuing our work on rescue and relief," Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal Army spokesman told AFP, adding that four helicopters had been deployed.
"We do not have any new information on the five missing," he added.
About 150 foreign trekkers are in the area, according to the Trekking Agencies' Association of Nepal, many on the popular Manaslu circuit trek.
"We are working with authorities to rescue those who are stranded because of the roads," the association's president Sagar Pandey said.
Authorities were also delivering aid to affected communities, with many residents fleeing their homes on Sunday morning as the torrent hit.
The flood also struck hydropower plants, according to the national disaster agency.
"I screamed out loud to get people out. Just a few minutes after people ran out the flood crashed through," local resident Indra Bahadur Gurung said.
"We have always lived here, and find it difficult to leave. I hope the government will manage something safe for us soon."
'REDUCING FUTURE RISKS'
Preliminary data suggests that a landslide had dammed the river. It then burst, with the water surging downstream.
"The government has already begun taking the necessary steps to restore normal life," Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a post on social media late Sunday.
He urged residents to stay in safe locations and to avoid travel on risky roads and bridges.
Nepal is still recovering from devastating floods on August 26, triggered by a mountain glacial collapse, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.
Shah told the United Nations last month that the August flooding "was a warning to the world" about the rising dangers of climate change.
Basanta Raj Adhikari, director at the Centre for Disaster Studies at Tribhuvan University, said that the latest flood showed the need for better monitoring.

"The frequency of the disasters is dangerous... it shows we need to go beyond our traditional river-level based early warning systems," Adhikari said, suggesting satellite images and seismometers could help detect events earlier.

The Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said Sunday that the floods highlighted the "range of hazards capable of generating destructive floods" in Himalayan river systems.
"Understanding what triggered this flood will be critical for reducing future risks and strengthening resilience," the centre's director general Pema Gyamtsho said in the statement.
Heavy rainfall in late September also triggered floods and landslides, killing at least 21 people, according to the disaster agency.

168065509b29f15b: JAKARTA: Indonesia will not declare its prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster for now, saying it remains capable of managing the crisis despite concerns over transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia.

Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Dudung Abdurachman said the decision was made at a limited cabinet meeting chaired by President Prabowo Subianto at the Presidential Palace here on Monday.
"Not yet, not yet. We are still capable of handling it," he told reporters after the meeting.
Dudung said offers of international assistance were not discussed, although he acknowledged concerns from neighbouring countries over the haze.
"There have indeed been responses from other countries regarding these forest fires, but we have made maximum efforts," he said, expressing hope that the situation could be resolved soon.
On Oct 8, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had contacted Prabowo about the haze and conveyed Malaysia's readiness to help to combat the fires.
Meanwhile, Dudung said Prabowo had directed firefighting efforts to focus on Tanjung Puting National Park and other affected areas in Central Kalimantan, as well as South Sumatra.
"Tanjung Puting and areas surrounding the national park must be protected because there is wildlife there," he said.
The park is internationally known for its orangutan conservation and rehabilitation programmes.

Earlier today, House of Representatives Commission IV member Daniel Johan has urged the government to declare the prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster and remain open to international assistance, including Malaysia's offer of firefighting support.
Daniel said the scale of the crisis required regional cooperation and that accepting foreign help should not be viewed as a sign of weakness.

Meanwhile, Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni warned that authorities must remain on high alert for another month, with natural rainfall not expected in parts of Indonesia until mid-November or even December.

During an inspection of firefighting operations at the Liang Anggang Protected Forest in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, he said the government was preparing to suspend or revoke the business permits of another five or six companies over fire-related violations.
Action had been taken against 26 companies, including five forestry concession holders in Kalimantan whose permits were revoked on Sept 21, he said.
The concession covered about 92,464 hectares, of which approximately 1,169 hectares had been affected by fires.
ae4fce27e96385b9: PETALING JAYA: Courts have the discretion to decide whether an accused person should remain under detention or be granted bail while awaiting the conclusion of their trial, says home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

In a written parliamentary reply, Saifuddin said decisions on continued detention or bail in cases in which charges had been filed but trials remained incomplete were made by the court in accordance with applicable laws.

“The home ministry, through the prisons department and the police, always takes seriously the management of remand detainees. The government is committed to upholding individual human rights and the principle of justice under the law.

“On the proposal to review remand periods for protracted cases, the ministry wishes to clarify that the power to fix remand periods falls entirely under the jurisdiction of the judiciary, among others under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code or the relevant special procedural laws.

“For cases where charges have been filed in court but the trial is not yet complete, re-detention or denial of bail (unbailable or non-bailable) is also at the court’s discretion under the applicable laws.”

He added that the police apply for remand based on investigative needs, while the magistrate or judge assesses and decides on a reasonable remand period according to the principle of balancing individual liberty with the interests of criminal investigation.
Saifuddin added that the government remained open to reviewing laws and standard operating procedures to safeguard detainees’ human rights and address overcrowding in prisons.
Among the measures being pursued were the Licensed Prisoner Release Programme, Compulsory Attendance Orders (PKW) and the parole system, which aim to reduce reliance on physical detention.
He was responding to a question from Khlir Nor (PN-Ketereh) about whether the government was prepared to review remand periods for cases that had yet to be decided by the courts.
Khlir said this would uphold justice and human rights, as well as reduce overcrowding in prisons.
Last month, Chief Justice Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh voiced concerns over some accused persons having to wait for more than two years under remand before their cases are heard in court.
In a speech at a recent Johor Bar dinner, he said it was “fundamentally unjust” that an accused person should wait in remand for more than two years before the matter is heard.
Wan Farid said the courts' delay effectively punished these accused persons before any verdict is delivered, adding that this must not continue.
In August, Sinar Harian reported that an Orang Asli man charged with murder was freed after spending nine years under remand, with his trial still at the prosecution stage.
1d5c3f17d558a1dc: PUTRAJAYA: Technical assessments and inspections of aging utilities in sinkhole-prone areas must be conducted before local authorities approve any development, the Housing and Local Government Ministry said.
The ministry said the decision was made at the 51st National Physical Planning Council (NPPC) meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"This approach is crucial to ensure public safety and geological risks are addressed from the early stages of development planning," the ministry said in a statement.

The ministry said NPPC also urged state governments to improve the provision of quality public open spaces and expedite their gazettement to ensure public access to safe and comfortable recreational areas, while promoting healthy lifestyles and strengthening community interaction.
It also approved the Fifth National Physical Plan (RFN5) and the Third National Urbanisation Policy (DPN3) as strategic frameworks for the country's physical and urban development.

RFN5 is the country's highest-level spatial planning document, covering Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Labuan until 2040. It focuses on sustainable land use, natural resource conservation and greater resilience to climate change and disasters.

Its targets include implementing smart city initiatives across 115 local authorities, maintaining at least 50 per cent forest cover and providing 1.6 million hectares of potential land to support economic growth.

DPN3, which runs until 2035, covers 203 cities under 101 local authorities in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. It aims to ensure urban growth is planned in a more structured, inclusive and sustainable manner, taking into account demographic, economic and technological changes, as well as climate change challenges.
The ministry said the council also considered the Putrajaya Structure Plan 2050 draft, which outlines the development direction for the national administrative centre.
The plan includes a target population of 305,000, the provision of 83,438 housing units, achieving carbon neutrality and the use of artificial intelligence in urban management.

The meeting also agreed to the Perlis State Structure Plan 2040, which outlines development strategies including the Perlis Inland Port, the Chuping Valley Industrial Area and the strengthening of the state's granary areas.

"Overall, the decisions of the 51st NPPC reinforce the government's commitment to ensuring the country's physical and urban development is planned, sustainable, inclusive, resilient and responsive to future changes, in line with the Malaysia Madani aspirations," the ministry said.
47ca11c2b31abef8: PETALING JAYA: Any proposed legislation to tackle transboundary haze must consider several factors, including its effectiveness, diplomatic implications, burden of proof, and whether the law could be enforced, the Dewan Rakyat was told.

“The effectiveness of a law, however, does not rest on its enactment alone, but the ability to gather evidence, carry out an investigation, and fortify laws outside of Malaysia’s jurisdiction,” he said in a parliamentary reply.

He was responding to Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who wanted to know if the government was reconsidering a Transboundary Haze Act or enacting a Clean Air Act following an emergency declared in Serian, Sarawak, last month.
He said transboundary haze was becoming more challenging because of several factors, including climate variability, long dry spells, and agricultural practices.
Last month, it was reported that Kurup’s ministry was looking to draft specific legislation to address transboundary haze, similar to the approach implemented by Singapore.
G Pubadi, the undersecretary of the ministry’s environmental management division, said they were examining the existing mechanisms in Singapore to draft a specific Act to address the haze.

While he did not specify which Singaporean mechanism he was referring to, the republic’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014 gave it legal powers to act against companies whose activities outside Singapore cause or contribute to haze in the city-state.
On Sept 17, the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) urged the government to enact a Clean Air Act to set legally binding air quality standards and protect public health.
The US enacted a Clean Air Act in 1963 to control air pollution and protect public health and the environment.
de69746aabbc012a: For over a decade now, the only "official" way to play Hideo Kojima's cult classic, P.T.—the long-discontinued "playable trailer" for Kojima's canceled "Silent Hills" project—has been via one of the increasingly rare PlayStation 4s that previously downloaded a copy during its monthslong availability window. Now, though, one coder is helping to preserve the game with a porting tool that builds a playable x86 PC executable from the original PS4 files.

Coder Lorean Xavier said he was inspired to work on the "P.T. for PC" project "because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on consoles that still have it installed." The open source porting effort rebuilds the P.T. engine in C++ and Vulkan, using the original files from the PS4 game to re-create "every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene," according to its GitHub listing. That means players without their own legitimate decrypted copy of the original P.T. will have to track one down in order to generate a playable PC version.

The reliance on real P.T. files makes this port more authentic than previous hobbyist efforts to re-create the look and feel of P.T. for a PC audience. And while PS4 emulators recently reached a point where they could run P.T. completely, this native port also sports extra features, like upscaling and frame-generation, a camera mode, experimental third-person and VR support, and a "museum" section where you can look at and listen to in-game assets (including "unused content").
dc6132295c40c733: ON Nov 19, expect a special government text message to pop out of your handphone screens. The message may "warn" you of an impending "natural disaster" near your area or residence.

You might also be advised to "immediately evacuate" your homes and proceed to the nearest shelter. Don't be alarmed: the message is a test from the Cell Broadcast System (CBS), a national disaster warning system that is undergoing pilot testing.
Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, the CBS transmits disaster alerts directly to handphones in affected areas.
Circumventing handphone numbers, SMS or Internet connection, the CBS will soon replace the existing SMS-based disaster warning system to provide faster and precise alerts.

As of 2025, the United Nations reported that 44 countries have adopted mobile-based public warning systems for earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, wildfires, severe storms and other emergencies. Malaysia's current system transmits targeted flood-warning SMS through the National Disaster Management Agency and telecommunications companies.
The CBS is technically sound, able to improve the speed in issuing alerts on emergencies.

The key issue is whether the government can connect hazard monitoring, accurate location targeting, telecommunications networks and clear instructions into a single and reliable national warning system.
From a technical standpoint, the CBS technology can blast an alert to all compatible handphones rather than send individual messages.

While the CBS can penetrate heavy voice and data traffic, it still depends on functioning mobile network infrastructure, though no special app is required. The challenge is rural coverage, raising public trust and awareness, and backup distribution methods in areas with poor coverage.
The CBS must also be able to send alerts in Bahasa Malaysia and English, and local dialects when necessary, while clearly distinguishing between advisories, imminent threats and evacuation orders.
The CBS should also accommodate individuals with visual, hearing or reading disabilities, which may require tailored video messages or other formats.
The Nov 19 pilot may launch in high-risk areas, such as flood-prone parts of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Kelantan and Pahang.

Malaysians know that skies can be clear and sunny and rivers calm, but floods can strike rapidly, making the CBS crucial for delivering timely warnings. The value of the CBS lies in its targeted warnings, giving families precious minutes to seek shelter, help vulnerable residents and allow authorities to respond effectively.
The CBS must complement a culture of preparedness rather than create a false sense of security as its usefulness depends on reception, understanding and action.
Ultimately, the CBS should not be judged by daily emergencies but by whether we are ready to act when disasters strike.
02600e82c18bb9a2: KUALA LUMPUR: Four men and a woman from Malaysia have been arrested at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, Japan, for attempting to smuggle about 5kg of cocaine worth 120 million yen (RM3.1 million), hidden beneath shoe insoles, on Saturday.

b865794ab8dffb03: AMD is expanding its rack-scale AI lineup with a design to run AI agents, offering CPU-only configurations or integrated CPU/GPU deployments, and liquid-cooled or air-cooled versions. Revealed at the Open Compute Project (OCP) Summit 2026 in San Jose, California, the chipmaker's new rack reference design is named Helion, while its existing system carries the moniker Helios, which we can't help feeling is inviting confusion a little. Helion offers an OCP-compliant blueprint for agentic AI infrastructure built around AMD's CPUs and accelerators. AMD launched Helios earlier this year for frontier-scale AI training and large-scale inference. Helion's enterprise configuration instead combines agent execution and inference within a single rack. Customers can opt for a CPU-only hyperscale configuration or an enterprise configuration with a mix of CPU and GPU blades. Depending on configuration, AMD advertises up to 32,768 of AMD's "Zen 6" CPU cores, delivered via compute nodes fitted with 256-core versions of its Venice Epyc processor, up to 16 of its Instinct MI350P GPU accelerators, and up to 102 Tbps of networking bandwidth. The CPU-only hyperscale version offers dedicated capacity for agent execution and connections to separate model inference infrastructure, while the enterprise configuration combines agent execution, GPU inference, and supporting workloads in one rack. Both configurations offer dense, balanced, or high-performance CPU blades. For dense deployments, EPYC 9006 chips rated at 400 W are used, while performance blades sport a version of the chip with just 96 cores but clocked at 5 GHz. Balanced blades use 256-core processors rated at 600 W. There are also GPU inference blades, with eight Instinct MI350P GPUs in a 5U server, plus general-purpose blades, intended for database and storage servers or technical compute workloads. AMD SVP for Compute and Enterprise AI Dan McNamara said agentic AI is not a single workload, spanning enterprise applications and complex workflows, each with different compute requirements. "To do that takes optimized compute and infrastructure that can adapt to different workloads. With AMD Helion, we are bringing Epyc performance, open software and flexible rack designs together so our partners can build systems around customer needs and make efficient use of available power," he added. AMD says it plans to contribute the Helion specifications to OCP, making them available to the community for further development and adoption. Partner-built Helion configurations are scheduled for November 2026. In its announcement, AMD cites Cisco, Dell, HPE, Foxconn, Lenovo, Supermicro, and others as on board with the new kit. ®
a2d36b84ac35c3c1: LONDON: Iran's Revolutionary Guards "almost certainly directed" a major scare at a UK airbase used by the US military for its war in Iran, Britain's prime minister Andy Burnham said Monday.
The US abruptly withdrew all its B-1 bombers from Royal Air Force Fairford last week after the mysterious incident at the base on Sept 27.
Burnham told parliament that Britain's assessment of the incident was that it "is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard".
"We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams," he warned.
The foreign office confirmed in a statement Monday that Iran's ambassador to the UK had been summoned for talks.

"We are also announcing the designation of two Iranian nationals for their role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime, with the clear intent of threatening, planning or conducting attacks overseas," foreign minister Ed Miliband said.

Speculation has swirled about the incident since police were called to the base in southwest England on Sept 27 after a local farmer reported a group of men with several white vans engaged in "suspicious" activity.
Despite a major counter-terrorism probe, seven suspects arrested in the days following, including a British-Iranian national, have all since been released on bail. None has been charged.
The incident was declared "major" by British authorities and triggered the evacuation of a nearby village.
But the source and nature of the threat have remained shrouded in mystery.
Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans but did recover some petrol, according to officials.

Miliband said the UK had already "designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under our new state threats powers and imposed major sanctions on those responsible for Iran's malign activity".
f70aac8008be7b54: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is seeking greater foreign investment and technology transfers to develop its rare earth industry and tap mineral resources estimated to be worth RM747.2 billion.

1931178fef134845: KUALA LUMPUR: The iron and steel sector is among the industries most frequently affected by dumped imports, with the government investigating products from six countries and territories to protect local manufacturers from unfair trade practices.

"These products are generally intermediate inputs in production chains rather than finished products or cheap consumer goods sold directly to consumers," he said in a written parliamentary reply.

05fa8fe1b891246b: KYIV: Ukraine on Monday passed legislation protecting the rights of national minorities, in a move expected to remove a major stumbling block to the country's EU ambitions.

Hungary had been blocking the opening of so-called negotiation "clusters" – policy areas with which EU candidates must align their laws – accusing Kyiv of failing to protect the rights of Ukraine's Hungarian minority.
Ukraine has long said it respected minority rights but nonetheless negotiated with Budapest over a possible law in a bid to accelerate its EU bid.
Kyiv's parliament voted Monday to pass the legislation, which President Volodymyr Zelensky then signed into law, his office said.
"A Ukrainian law has been passed that ensures the rights of national minorities without compromising the status of the Ukrainian language," the parliamentary press service said.
The law, it added, would "expand opportunities for the use of the languages of national minorities of Ukraine that are official languages of the European Union" in the educational system.
Hungary's foreign minister Anita Orban commended the move, saying it was "a necessary condition" for Hungary to agree to the opening of new EU talks.
Hungarian prime minister Peter Magyar said the approval of the law was a "good sign".
Magyar was elected earlier this year, ending the long rule of nationalist Viktor Orban, who had close relations with Russia.

"There is still a great deal to be done to ensure that relations improve once again and that trust is restored on both sides, but I believe that the leaderships of both countries have taken the first steps towards resolving the situation," Magyar said.
The status of the Hungarian-speaking minority in western Ukraine has long caused tensions between the neighbours.
Budapest had blocked Ukraine's EU membership bid, officially submitted days after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The EU's enlargement commissioner Marta Kos hailed the new law as "crucial to keep reforms moving."
"Tomorrow, we plan to open two more negotiating clusters on Ukraine's EU path," she added.
c96111813e453087: JAKARTA: Indonesia tidak akan mengisytiharkan kebakaran hutan dan tanah yang berlarutan di negara itu sebagai bencana nasional buat masa ini, menyatakan kerajaannya masih berupaya menangani krisis itu.

Menteri Penyelaras Hal Ehwal Politik dan Keselamatan Dudung Abdurachman berkata, keputusan itu dicapai pada mesyuarat Kabinet terhad yang dipengerusikan Presiden Prabowo Subianto di Istana Merdeka di Jakarta hari ini.
“Belum lagi, belum lagi. Kami masih berupaya menanganinya,” katanya kepada pemberita selepas mesyuarat.
Dudung berkata, tawaran bantuan antarabangsa tidak dibincangkan dalam mesyuarat itu, sambil mengakui kebimbangan berhubung jerebu merentas sempadan yang menjejaskan negara jiran, termasuk Malaysia.
“Memang ada maklum balas daripada negara lain berhubung kebakaran hutan ini, namun kita telah berusaha secara maksimum,” katanya sambil menzahirkan harapan agar situasi itu dapat diselesaikan segera.
Pada 8 Okt, Perdana Menteri Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim berkata, beliau telah menghubungi Prabowo berhubung isu jerebu dan menyampaikan kesediaan Malaysia untuk membantu memadamkan kebakaran.
Sementara itu, Dudung berkata, Prabowo telah mengarahkan usaha pemadaman kebakaran ditumpukan di Taman Negara Tanjung Puting dan kawasan terjejas lain di Kalimantan Tengah, serta Sumatera Selatan.
“Tanjung Puting dan kawasan di sekitar taman negara itu mesti dilindungi kerana terdapat hidupan liar di sana,” katanya.
Taman negara berkenaan terkenal di peringkat antarabangsa bagi program pemuliharaan dan rehabilitasi orang utan.

Awal hari ini, Ahli Suruhanjaya Keempat Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat (DPR) Daniel Johan menggesa kerajaan mengisytiharkan kebakaran hutan dan tanah yang berlarutan itu sebagai bencana nasional serta bersikap terbuka terhadap bantuan antarabangsa, termasuk tawaran sokongan pemadaman kebakaran daripada Malaysia.
Daniel berkata, skala krisis itu memerlukan kerjasama serantau dan menerima bantuan luar tidak sepatutnya dilihat sebagai satu kelemahan.

Sementara itu, Menteri Perhutanan Raja Juli Antoni memberi amaran bahawa pihak berkuasa mesti kekal berada dalam keadaan berjaga-jaga untuk tempoh sebulan lagi, memandangkan hujan tidak dijangka melanda beberapa bahagian di Indonesia sehingga pertengahan November atau Disember.

Semasa pemeriksaan operasi pemadaman kebakaran di Hutan Simpan Liang Anggang di Banjarbaru, Kalimantan Selatan pada Isnin, beliau berkata, kerajaan sedang bersiap sedia untuk menggantung atau membatalkan lesen perniagaan lima atau enam lagi syarikat berikutan pelanggaran berkaitan kebakaran.
Tindakan telah diambil terhadap 26 syarikat, termasuk lima pemegang konsesi perhutanan di Kalimantan yang lesen mereka dibatalkan pada 21 Sept, katanya.
Konsesi berkenaan merangkumi kira-kira 92,464 hektar, dengan anggaran 1,169 hektar daripadanya terjejas akibat kebakaran.
4b8bbcf9534926b3: KAJANG: The search and rescue operation for a man believed to have been swept away by river currents in Sungai Chuah yesterday was suspended this afternoon following heavy rain.

fd8c3153b84ca74c: JAPANESE Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration is ramping up efforts to shed its growth and easy money image through changes in rhetoric, a move that may backfire unless it is met with action such as substantial cuts to spending.

With major economies facing increased scrutiny from bond investors worried about rising inflation and yields, a lack of clarity on funding could cause another bond selloff in Japan given its US$7 trillion debt pile that is the biggest among advanced nations.
Takaichi vowed to cap new debt issuance around 40 trillion yen, even as spending requests for next year's budget hit a record 143 trillion yen.
A planned two-year sales tax cut would also cost roughly 4 trillion yen per year.
The government hopes to fill the gap by tapping rising tax revenues and state funds, a tricky task that would still pump money and inflationary pressures into the economy, analysts say.
"Markets look at the substance of policy and won't believe words alone," said Eiji Doke, chief bond strategist at SBI Securities.
"It's not that market players misunderstand Takaichi's policies. Rather, what they're watching is completely different from what the administration is trying to do."
Takaichi became premier in October last year with a pledge to ramp up spending to spur growth. She filled government panels with her reflationist aides to promote loose fiscal policy.
"Only by strengthening the economy would Japan achieve fiscal sustainability," she said in a policy speech back then in explaining her plan to compile a big spending package.

The administration's hefty fuel subsidies, a tax-cut pledge and big investment plans cemented market perceptions of its policies being reflationary as the economy struggled to recover from decades of low growth and low inflation.
But rising bond yields have become constraints on Takaichi's ambitions, forcing her administration to change its language.
"Fiscal sustainability is a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," she told Parliament last Monday.
She also pledged to "control" bond issuance and enhance communication with markets in a sign of the administration's sensitivity to rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields.
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield has hit multi-decade highs on concern Takaichi's spending plans may lead to increased debt issuance and strain Japan's worsening finances.

Efforts to phase out the administration's reflationist image geared up after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's calls in August for Japan to depart from Abenomics — a mix of loose fiscal and monetary steps deployed by former premier Shinzo Abe to beat deflation.
Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama led the communication shift.
In a recent media interview, she said the government decided around late August to recalibrate its messaging to reassure markets Takaichi was not pursuing reflationary policies.
Soon after, reflationist aides began to change tone.
Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi, for one, said on Sept 25 that the phase of Abenomics-style reflationary policies was over.
Former Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, who also sits on a government panel, also said last month reflationist policies "have no place in Japan now".
The shift in tone occurred at the BOJ, too.
Ayano Sato, a reflationist board member picked by Takaichi, told Kyodo News on Wednesday that she supports raising rates.
The government began to stress its spending plans are aimed at boosting supply capacity rather than reflating growth.
Markets are focusing on whether Takaichi will meet words with action as the government drafts next fiscal year's budget.

Katayama vowed to tap unused funds and identify wasteful spending to seek revenues under Japan's equivalent of the US Department of Government Efficiency initiative, focusing on the 7 trillion yen pooled by about 200 state funds.
But tapping such funds for spending is unsustainable and could stimulate the economy, running counter to the BOJ's efforts to curb inflation with rate hikes, some analysts say.
Former BOJ board member Asahi Noguchi, known as a reflationist, said now was the time to avoid boosting demand and causing bond yield rises that crowd out private investment.
"The administration probably didn't have a coherent view, with some clinging to the legacy of Abenomics, though that seems to have changed," he said.
"The key is to cut wasteful spending and convince markets Japan is serious about fiscal reform."

0cd29c134d84bf95: THE message was clear as United States Vice-President JD Vance shook hands in his native Ohio with a woman wearing a "Vance 2028" cap — at least from his supporter's perspective.

Donald Trump's deputy has yet to declare that he will run for the White House in two years' time. But what was supposed to be a campaign rally on Friday for Republican candidates in November's US midterm elections in Lima, Ohio, looked a lot more like a Vance rally.
With a theatrical flourish, Vance descended from the steps of Air Force Two, the vice-presidential jet, and received a rapturous reception as he entered the event in a flag-draped airport hangar.
"Man, it feels good to be home," Vance said to cheers.
Unusually for Vance on the campaign trail, he then went down to greet the crowd in person — shaking hands, patting arms and meeting the lady with the black pro-Vance hat.
There's just one problem for Vance: the midterms themselves.
Polls show Trump's unpopularity, the Iran war and the price of living could cost Republicans their majority in Congress.
And Ohio, which voted for Trump in the last three presidential elections, has turned from a stronghold into one of the tightest electoral battlegrounds for the Nov 3 vote.
There are nail-biting races for Vance's old senate seat, currently held by Jon Husted, and for the governorship of Ohio, where former Republican presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is standing.
In a sign of Republican concerns, Vance's visit comes days after Trump travelled to the state and the 80-year-old president is due back there next week.
For Trump, losing control of Congress could mean he spends his last two years in office battling multiple Democrat-led investigations.
For Vance, losing Ohio could seriously damage a political brand that was largely built on the blue-collar roots in the state described in his bestselling memoir "Hillbilly Elegy".

"I think it has nothing to do with 2028," he insisted to reporters when asked how important it was to win Ohio for Republicans as he looked to a presidential run. "It has to do with how we're going to govern our country over the next two years, the next 10 years."
Despite Vance's comments, the race for 2028 will effectively start the day after the midterms.
While Vance is widely considered the frontrunner to be Trump's heir, he's made no announcement yet and it's far from a done deal.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said he won't run against Vance, but his speech on western civilisation against the backdrop of the Acropolis in Athens was widely seen as a pitch for the job.
There is a growing buzz around the youthful vice-president.
Like any good candidate, Vance is increasingly bringing his family on the stump.
The 42-year-old took his wife Usha, three of their four children and their dog Atlas on Air Force Two for the flight to Cincinnati, where Vance cast an early vote for the midterms.
Vance is also raising money. His role as the finance chair of the Republican National Committee puts him at the centre of a nexus of wealthy donors.
Politically, Vance is quietly trying to exorcise the vice-president's curse of being tied to the policies of the outgoing president — one that Kamala Harris suffered from in 2024.
His speeches have subtly positioned him as more conscious of the financial woes of US families, even as Trump dismisses what he calls the "affordability hoax".
Staking out his own positions also helps counter the idea that Vance is a political shape-shifter — he once compared Trump to Hitler before becoming his vice-president.

The recent Catholic convert on Friday sought to distance himself from another key administration figure, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, over the announcement that a US military firing squad execution would be livestreamed.

"I've seen these announcements. I don't know that that's going to happen," Vance told a reporter travelling with him on Friday, adding that if it was going to be "through livestream, I'm not going to be watching it".
The writer is from AFP

aece79373b108563: PETALING JAYA: The Women’s Aid Organisation (WAO) has called for femicide to be recognised within Malaysia’s legal framework and for a systematic mechanism to record, monitor and analyse the gender-related killings of women and girls.
Several women and girls have been killed between January and October in cases reported in Batu Pahat, Butterworth, Kepong, Kulim, Ketereh, Kuantan and Yong Peng.
The cases included the recent deaths of a 19-year-old woman in Kuantan, Pahang, and a 16-year-old schoolgirl in Yong Peng, Johor.

In a statement, WAO said Malaysia lacks a specific legal or statistical category for femicide, which refers to the intentional killing of women and girls with a gender-related motive, often linked to misogyny, discrimination, unequal power relations, or gender-based violence.

It said identifying and monitoring the gender-related deaths of women and girls was crucial as it would help highlight patterns, understand risk factors, and assist in forming evidence-based policies and prevention measures.

The group said femicide was linked to wider gender inequalities and harmful attitudes, including misogyny, possessiveness, entitlement, victim-blaming, and the normalisation of violence against women.

“Prevention must begin early through education on consent, empathy, respect, equality and healthy relationships, alongside stronger institutional responses to warning signs of abuse and appropriate protection for those at risk.
“The killing of women and girls must not be treated as isolated incidents. Every case should compel us to examine whether earlier intervention could have prevented the loss of life.
“Women and girls have the right to live free from violence. We must act now to strengthen protection and prevention before more lives are lost,” it said.

While not every killing of a woman could be classified as femicide, WAO said, recurring cases involving intimate partners, family members, and men known to the victims raised serious concerns about the safety of women and girls.

The group also highlighted gaps in the Domestic Violence Act 1994, particularly in protecting survivors of abuse in non-marital intimate relationships, such as those involving boyfriends and girlfriends.
It urged the government to expand the Act to cover non-marital intimate partner violence and strengthen protection orders to ensure survivors could obtain timely protection.

It also called on schools to strengthen mechanisms for identifying warning signs of gender-based violence, including threats, harassment, stalking, and coercive control, with appropriate referral and safety measures.
a28af2371faff12a: Microsoft has closed a loophole that let users sidestep the need for an account during setup for consumer versions of Windows 11. If users clicked "Learn More" when the setup process prompted for a Microsoft account, the Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE) skipped directly to the point where they just had to enter a name and password. Windows prodder "Bob Pony," who first documented the loophole, reported its removal. We tried the original trick on real Intel hardware and found it was possible to skip the Microsoft account requirement by clicking a link, but no longer. Other hacks – for those who dare to use unofficial Windows setup routes – still exist, though they are beyond the skill set of the average user. Microsoft requires an account during initial setup of Windows 11 Home and Pro for personal use. For consumers, using Windows 11 without an account can be tricky because services such as OneDrive require authentication. Microsoft is far from the only operating system vendor to demand an account during setup, but many Linux distributions, by contrast, don't require one. According to Bob Pony, the loophole was "quietly patched server side," which makes sense. Microsoft was hardly likely to leave it flapping open for long. Microsoft has won this round of account workaround Whac-a-Mole, though another bypass may yet pop up. ®
f1278fdef0000313: PASIR MAS: A Form Two student's body appeared to be smoking after he was struck by lightning while fishing in a padi field in Kampung Tasek Berangan here around 4.30pm today, his cousin recalled.
"When the lightning struck, all four of us fell backwards, and at that moment, I saw Ziad's body smoking," said Haziq Qayyum Rosli, 12.
Haziq is the cousin of Muhammad Ziad Zikri Abdul Hadi, who was killed in the incident.
Haziq, who sustained an injury to the back of his right shoulder, said they were walking towards their motorcycles to return home due to sudden heavy rain when the incident happened.

"We arrived at the padi field at 4pm. But it suddenly rained and I asked Ziad and our other friend if we could go home because I was worried the rain would get heavier. At that time, there was no lightning yet.
"However, Ziad asked us to be patient as we had just arrived and he had already caught two fish, so he still wanted to continue fishing.
"At that moment (when lightning striked), I saw Ziad's body smoking, and we ran home to inform Ziad's father," he said when met here.
Haziq said he initially thought Ziad had only fainted, before others arrived and told them that he had died.
"The four of us liked fishing at that spot and never expected this to happen.
"I am very sad because the four of us were so close," he said.

Earlier, Ziad's father, Abdul Hadi Abdul Ghani, 60, said he rushed to the padi field and cradled his son after learning that the boy had been struck by lightning, only to find that he was already dead.
Recounting the incident, Hadi said he had been asleep at home when his youngest of five children went fishing with a friend and cousin.
Ziad was a student at SMK Sri Kiambang here. His body is expected to be buried tomorrow morning.
c51c6bb06fc006e1: Formula 1’s lengthy 2026 season is entering its final stretch. The sport took to the floodlit streets of Singapore on Sunday night, but Saturday saw action, too; this Grand Prix weekend was also the final of six sprints this year. The night race might be one of modern F1’s greatest spectacles. From overhead shots, the track becomes a bright, illuminated ribbon among the looming darkness of the city-state’s overpasses and skyscrapers. At ground level, the cars shower glittering sparks from their titanium skid blocks as the drivers flirt with how close they can get to the walls. As tracks go, the 90-degree turns and concrete barrier-lined streets were a world away from the abrasive tarmac and ample runoff of Malaysia last time out. But the tropical heat and humidity were a constant given both locations’ proximity to the equator.

In Malaysia (which was still technically the Bahrain GP), a pre-race downpour disrupted things mightily. On Saturday morning in Singapore, shortly before the start of the sprint, it seemed history was about to rhyme when the skies opened. With standing water in places on the track, the sprint was delayed by 30 minutes. The sprint format, where a short extra race replaces a practice session a day before the main event, is unloved by the drivers and teams. For one thing, there’s little prestige in winning Saturday’s sprint. And with qualifying just a few hours later, risk-taking is discouraged lest one wreck the car and ruin Sunday’s race a day early.

Oh no, not again! Credit: Mark Thompson/Getty Images And in Singapore, like most street circuits, the proximity of the unyielding barriers that line the track means there are real, punishing consequences for getting it even a little wrong.
57480870ed2ad972: JAKARTA: Indonesia will not declare its prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster for now, saying it remains capable of handling the crisis.

Coordinating minister for political and security affairs Dudung Abdurachman said the decision was made at a limited cabinet meeting chaired by President Prabowo Subianto at the Presidential Palace in Jakarta on Monday.
“Not yet, not yet. We are still capable of handling it,” he told reporters after the meeting.
Dudung said offers of international assistance were not discussed at the meeting, while acknowledging concerns over transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia.
“There have indeed been responses from other countries regarding these forest fires, but we have made maximum efforts,” he said, expressing hope that the situation could be resolved soon.
On Oct 8, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had contacted Prabowo about the haze and conveyed Malaysia’s readiness to help to combat the fires.
Meanwhile, Dudung said Prabowo had directed firefighting efforts to focus on Tanjung Puting National Park and other affected areas in Central Kalimantan, as well as South Sumatra.
“Tanjung Puting and areas surrounding the national park must be protected because there is wildlife there,” he said.
The park is internationally known for its orangutan conservation and rehabilitation programmes.

Earlier on Monday, House of Representatives (DPR) Commission IV member Daniel Johan urged the government to declare the prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster and remain open to international assistance, including Malaysia’s offer of firefighting support.
Daniel said the scale of the crisis required regional cooperation and that accepting foreign help should not be viewed as a sign of weakness.

Meanwhile, forestry minister Raja Juli Antoni warned that authorities must remain on high alert for another month, with natural rainfall not expected in parts of Indonesia until mid-November or even December.

During an inspection of firefighting operations at the Liang Anggang Protected Forest in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, on Monday, he said the government was preparing to suspend or revoke the business permits of another five or six companies over fire-related violations.

Action had been taken against 26 companies, including five forestry concession holders in Kalimantan whose permits were revoked on Sept 21, he said. The concession covered about 92,464 hectares, of which approximately 1,169 hectares had been affected by fires.
39e2c25d7ce7dd98: JOHOR BAHRU: The Johor education department has set up a special task force to monitor the haze situation and prepare standard operating procedures for school operations.

4811bcbd9efdb60c: PUTRAJAYA: Penilaian teknikal dan pemeriksaan utiliti usang di kawasan berisiko berlaku lubang benam perlu dilaksanakan sebelum sebarang kelulusan pembangunan diberikan oleh pihak berkuasa tempatan (PBT).

1003598713b7abba: KUANTAN: A university student lost RM32,115 after being duped by a scammer posing as a police officer who accused him of money laundering.

Azmi said the victim handed the items to a masked woman and was told not to inform his family or anyone else.

"Investigations revealed that the female suspect had been offered a job by the syndicate, which claimed she had been appointed as a member of the 'Police Special Actions Unit'.

35528abdf7376fcd: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia's energy minister on Monday said the country had been tested but would mount a "serious" response after a string of attacks on Riyadh's international airport by Yemen's Houthis that left 18 people dead.
Lethal airport strikes since last week have rocked the world's top oil exporter, which is pursuing an expensive economic reform drive aimed at attracting foreign investment.

Yemen's civil war, where a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis, has reignited months into the US-Iran conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.
"Energy security can't be taken for granted," Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh, as oil prices topped US$105 a barrel.
"The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious."
"For Saudi Arabia, these circumstances have tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience," he added.
On Saturday, Houthi strikes killed 13 people and wounded hundreds at King Khalid International Airport – the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade.
Four people died in earlier attacks on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh's outskirts on Monday.

CCTV footage of Saturday's attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden flash tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.
'The whole house shook'

The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats, and Australia's embassy warned its citizens in the city to shelter in place.

The Houthis on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the previous 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting Saudi transit hubs, calling them "a theatre of operations for our forces".
Hours later, the coalition said yet another projectile had struck Riyadh airport, sparking a fire, while air defences intercepted a missile nearby.
AFP journalists and locals reported hearing multiple blasts in the capital on Sunday.
"The whole house shook," said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the city's north.
Riyadh's airport was not the only one to suffer a deadly attack: early on Monday, officials said one person had been killed and 11 wounded in a strike on Dammam airport.
The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that it had also "intercepted and destroyed" a Houthi ballistic missile heading for the southern city of Khamis Mushait, home to a major military base.
Riyadh hosts a packed calendar of events at this time of year, including its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, which draws foreign leaders and business titans.
'Full-fledged war crime'
Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.

"Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it's simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves," said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.
The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday's attack a "full-fledged war crime" and vowed to "respond decisively".
The attack drew condemnation from the UN and leaders, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
Iran, which backs the Houthis, said Monday it was "deeply concerned" over the recent escalation.
Witnesses to Saturday's strike described chaos in the aftermath.

0576af9c91682f0d: NEW DELHI: Thousands of protesters marched in New Delhi on Monday demanding the resignation of India's election chief over alleged misconduct during a voter roll revision, the latest showdown with authorities in the heavily fortified capital.

Opposition parties and supporters of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party protest movement have taken to the streets in recent days, defying a strict security clampdown to demand a halt to the revision exercise and the resignation of the chief election commissioner.
"You can see how big the crowd is," demonstrator Abhay Aryan, 28, told AFP as protesters marched towards the Supreme Court, chanting slogans and waving placards.
"The government has to listen to the voice of the people."
Critics say the large-scale revision of electoral lists could benefit prime minister Narendra Modi's ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world's most populous nation, has denied wrongdoing.
A protester who gave his name as Mehvaish said he could no longer "tolerate the injustices" meted out by Modi's government.
"We want removal of this government (because) of all the injustices we have suffered in the past 12-13 years," he said.
"Now if they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?"

Rights advocates and critics say Modi's government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents – allegations the government rejects.
Thousands detained
Authorities deployed thousands of security personnel across central Delhi for a third straight day, erecting heavy metal barricades and closing key metro stations.
The protests on Monday were led by Rahul Gandhi of the main opposition Congress party, who waved a copy of the constitution as crowds cheered during the procession to the Supreme Court.
He later filed a writ petition in the court through his lawyer, challenging the voter revision exercise.
Public attention has also focused on the police response after a chaotic weekend in which thousands of protesters, including organisers, were detained, according to local media reports.
Most of those detained, including three top leaders of the "cockroach" movement, have since been released.
Opposition figures have accused authorities of trying to suppress dissent through mass detentions.
Parliamentarian John Brittas of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) alleged he was "manhandled, dragged, and assaulted" by police during Sunday's demonstrations.
"This is not merely an assault on an MP. It is an assault on democratic freedoms and the rule of law," Brittas said.
Police did not respond to questions on detentions or their actions during a news conference on Sunday.
Several journalists covering the protest said they were detained despite prominently displaying their press cards.
Nitin Katiyar, a digital journalist, told The Times of India newspaper police had punched him in the eye. AFP could not immediately verify his charge.
'Spirit of resistance'
Hundreds of yellow metal barricades were set up on roads leading to central Delhi, while six major metro stations remained shut.
The protests have become a major political challenge for Modi, drawing together opposition parties, student groups and activists angered by the voter roll revision.
The leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, which has millions of social media followers, have pledged to continue their protests until Kumar steps down.
They reiterated that pledge on Monday after Delhi Police announced that Jantar Mantar in the heart of Delhi was no longer designated as an official protest site.
"If Modi thinks taking away Jantar Mantar will put an end to protests, he is mistaken," the group's founder Abhijeet Dipke said on social media.
"Jantar Mantar is not just a location but a spirit of resistance that nobody can ever take away."
The revision of voter rolls that started last year has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to media reports.
Critics say the measure has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.
A senior minister from Modi's party accused Gandhi's Congress on Monday of trying to undermine legitimate electoral processes.
"By discrediting constitutional institutions (and) spreading chaos and riots on the streets, all that the Congress is seeking is to seize power," Shivraj Singh Chouhan told reporters.

c25f6308f79c3ce0: Yandex engineers are working to restore services after Ukraine launched drone strikes on three of its five Russian datacenters. The strikes began overnight on October 7-8, "seriously damaging" Yandex's Sasovo datacenter and leading to a total shutdown. Ukrainian drones struck again on the morning of October 9, targeting the company's Kaluga datacenter, resulting in part of its infrastructure being taken offline. Dima Pirogov, head of Yandex's fintech division, confirmed via Telegram on Sunday morning that a third strike targeted the company's Vladimir site, which supports Yandex Pay. A day later, services remain offline, although Pirogov said users' money is safe. "I'm very sorry I can't tell you yet that everything is working again," the exec wrote. "The team continues to restore services and is checking every step. When it comes to your money, it's important to us not just to restore Yandex Pay as quickly as possible, but also to ensure that everything is working reliably. "I understand that you're not waiting for words, but for access to your money. And I understand how hard it is to wait when you can't use it. We can't give you a precise timeline for the restoration yet, but we promise: we won't stop until the service is back online." Yandex Pay is the company's digital payments service. Users can make online and in-store purchases, pay in installments, and split bills with friends and family. It's also integrated into online shopping experiences. It is comparable to Apple Pay or Google Pay, while Yandex more broadly offers services similar to Google's. Yandex said engineers are prioritizing the most-used services, and reported that access to the Alice AI assistant, Mail, Maps, Search, and Taxi is being restored, but other features remain offline. The company's status page lists widespread outages across Yandex Cloud, its public cloud platform, following the attacks. Updates from the maintenance team describe partial availability despite the outage indicators. They suggest that some customers may be able to access certain features, such as Yandex Cloud Console and API, but availability remains inconsistent across the platform. In its most recent update, the company said: "The Yandex Cloud platform is still operating in a limited mode. Our specialists continue restoration work around the clock. The technical support team receives an increased number of requests, so the response time can be increased. "Our recommendations continue to be relevant. We recommend using alternative sites for hosting and reserving resources." Internet monitoring organization Netblocks reported that Yandex Cloud's network connectivity was at 30 percent of normal levels on October 11. Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelensky said the drone attacks were a response to Russia's own, which had targeted datacenters in Kyiv. The BBC reported that in September, Russian drone strikes targeted a business center in the capital city, killing four people and damaging a datacenter, which in turn resulted in around 100,000 households losing internet access. The attacks led to other knock-on effects, such as public transport boards not displaying information in Lutsk. Kyiv's attack on the Vladimir site on Sunday morning came hours after controversial comments from US president Donald Trump, who accused Zelensky of wanting "to make problems for the world" by continuing to attack Russian oil refineries. Trump went on to say that it was time for Ukraine to elect a new president after Zelensky said measures should not be taken that allow Russia to generate more revenue to fund its war. Zelensky was referring to a deal between Trump and Putin to release diesel from Russia to the US and the rest of the world. Later that day, the US president claimed Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" to halt attacks on each other's energy infrastructure. Kyiv said it was unaware of the agreement before Trump announced it on his social media platform, but was willing to halt attacks on Russian energy infrastructure if Moscow reciprocated. Russia launched a missile attack on a Ukrainian power plant hours later. ®

f930a62ec600c8bf: PHNOM PENH, Oct 12 — Tourists once stayed away during rainy seasons, but the Mekong region intends to woo them by turning its wet season into a major attraction that showcases its scenic beauty.
Governments across the Mekong region are also steering tourism toward the new trend of greener models to court eco-minded travellers and tap rural resources during the off-season.
From Cambodia and Myanmar to Vietnam, the lull monsoon season is slowly transforming into a vibrant tourism segment.

“This is the time when Cambodia reveals its most authentic and vibrant beauty. Flourishing nature, fresh greenery stretching across the country, clean air, and magnificent landscapes create rare and valuable experiences for visitors,” Cambodia Tourism Minister Huot Hak said at the Coastal Green Season Tourism Event 2026 in Kampot province in early October.

The monsoon unveils the Mekong region’s hidden scenic treasures. From May to October, the long rains add a fresh coat to the rural landscape — rain breathes new life into the rainforest, glistens the parched paddy fields, and once-dry rivers and ponds swell into picnic and rafting spots. And coastal areas come alive with cultural and traditional festivals.
Tourism industries are restructuring activities and launching targeted, tourist-centric events to attract visitors who would otherwise avoid travelling during the wet season.
Quang Ninh province in northern Vietnam is promoting year-round tourism built on night-time entertainment, festivals, and the spiritual appeal of its mountain and forest landscapes.
Farther south, Da Nang has moved beyond beach tourism to urban attractions, resorts, entertainment, and culture when the weather is unsuitable for swimming, reported news portal Vietnamnet.
Hanoi Tourism Association Vice Chairman Nguyen Tien Dat said the new concept does not mean ushering tourists to risky areas but restructuring tourism products.

“A rainy day is an opportunity for museum visits, heritage tours, culinary experiences, wellness, art or craft villages, while a beach itinerary can be replaced with a city tour, nature excursion, and community-based cultural activities,” he said, as reported by Vietnamnet.
The low season also offers advantages in service prices, less crowded spaces, and opportunities to organise more in-depth experiences, he said.
Tourists looking for economical travels would be pleased to know that overall travel costs drop by 30 to 50 per cent during the rainy season, according to the Vietnam Tourism website.
A boutique hotel in Hoi An, for instance, costs US$90 (RM368) in February but drops to US$35 in October. Halong Bay cruises are 40 per cent cheaper.
Authorities in Myanmar, one of South-east Asia’s untapped jewels, are encouraging travels during the monsoon to enjoy its pristine landscapes.

In picturesque Hpa-an, the capital of Kayin State, most hotels were fully booked as local visitors flocked to admire the region’s scenic landscapes during the season, according to state media The Global New Light of Myanmar.

Travel preferences are shifting across generations, with Gen Z and millennials — who are more environmentally conscious, budget-minded, and eager for adventure — leading the change, according to industry observers.
Tourism today is about more than generating revenue and welcoming visitors.
Modern-day tourism is closely linked to sustainability, the promotion of cultural heritage and values, and the upliftment of rural communities and economies — while ensuring environmental protection.

It generates income for craft makers, guesthouse owners, guides, motorcycle and bicycle rental operators, farmers, and traditional performers, boosting community enterprises, including those run by women.

Tourism supports jobs and growth, but also generates 7.3 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions, according to the World Travel and Tourism Council. A shift toward greener travel could help cut those emissions. — Bernama

273a91b33201d9e7: UCLA and Oracle have settled a dispute over a troubled ERP project originally budgeted at $120 million, with the vendor waiving $1.31 million in outstanding fees and granting $3.1 million in credits against future charges. In May, the University of California's Compliance and Audit Committee recommended a settlement [PDF] of UCLA's pre-litigation dispute with Oracle, which the Board of Regents approved. According to documents released in response to a California Public Records Act request, UCLA stopped paying its Oracle subscription in September 2024 over what it described as shortcomings in grants management functionality. UCLA and Oracle signed their first agreement relating to the project – called Ascend – in November 2017. The project had a revised go-live date of January 2025, but was paused in mid-2024. The settlement records UCLA's allegation that "the ERP Cloud Services did not perform as warranted in the Oracle Agreement." "The ERP Cloud Services lacked sufficient functionality to meet the University's requirements and could not be used by the University as expected," said the document, which was seen by The Register. It continued that "the University incurred costs and delays due to the ERP Cloud Services inability to meet the University's requirements." It added: "As a result, Oracle breached the Oracle Agreement." Under the settlement, UCLA agreed to pay Oracle $350,000 of the $1.66 million in outstanding invoices. Oracle then waived the remaining balance – $1.31 million – and credited $3.1 million against future Oracle fees. These credits expire at the end of May 2028. The agreement says the university should not make public statements about its terms, which are to remain confidential, although both parties acknowledged that UCLA is subject to the California Public Records Act. The Register has asked Oracle to comment. The settlement was obtained by California resident Eric Guyer, founder of independent Oracle cost consultancy Advizant. In a social media post, he said that the credits suggested UCLA would continue with the project in some form, with Oracle as the main vendor. Guyer suggested Oracle most likely discounted its software to win the "coveted" UCLA logo. He estimated the total subscription value at around $12 million over ten years. He said Oracle tends to move decisively when unpaid bills on clear contractual terms back it into a corner. "This is rare despite the lore of its litigious nature. Everyone has a line. In any case, UCLA's claim probably went to Oracle because it was the easiest to point a finger at: consultants sell effort, not outcomes, and internal staff can only be fired." However, he said the average customer should not conclude that claiming a breach and stopping payment is advisable. "It can be effective, but is an exceedingly painful path," he claimed. "In this rare case, Oracle agreed to eat some shit at the end of a poorly planned implementation in exchange for UCLA's silence in the fiercely competitive higher ed market. In other public implementation fights, Oracle struck first or countersued, with press releases to match." UCLA serves around 49,000 students and manages a budget of around $11 billion. A 2025 report [PDF] presented to the University of California Board of Regents' Finance and Capital Strategies Committee said that among the "Top Issues, Risks and Challenges" the UCLA project leadership faced was "Oracle's lack of responsiveness – particularly regarding licensing costs and support." It added that the project's original $120 million budget was revised down to $98.9 million, with $13.5 million remaining as of December 31, 2024. The report, covering the period through December 2024, said the project started in April 2018 and was originally expected to end in July 2020. The document described it as a "comprehensive business transformation initiative" to modernize the university's financial, budgetary, and research administration operations by moving to Oracle Cloud SaaS. It also included retrofitting any systems that connected with the main finance system. The procurement module, BruinBuy Plus, went live in January 2024, but the main "Oracle Financials go-live has been paused since August 2 [2024] and is undergoing program assessment," the document said. Among the mitigation plans in the review was to "finalize the decision on whether to continue with the current vendor or explore alternatives" based on a reassessment of the tool and provider. According to the settlement document, the University told Oracle via email on June 20, 2025 that the "University wanted to terminate the Ascend project and the ERP Cloud Services." In May, a spokesperson for UCLA said in a statement to The Register: "The University continues to evaluate the most effective path forward for financial systems modernization." Under the terms of the settlement agreement, the University and Oracle have agreed to make no further claims for damages related to the contract dispute, and neither has admitted liability. According to a report from campus newspaper Daily Bruin, UCLA was still using legacy financial systems software designed in the 1980s when the budget was just seven percent of its current size. It was a mainframe-based "ancient relic of a system," former project steering committee member Reem Hanna-Harwell told the newspaper. The Daily Bruin reported that at least $213 million had been spent and cited a May 2024 town hall presentation projecting total costs of roughly $286 million. ®
